facts.statement: Gloria Jean Siebrecht discovered the fossils in 1991 on the Blackfeet Indian Reservation.
facts.quote: The fossils were found in 1991 by Gloria Jean Siebrecht in the Blackfeet Indian Reservation

facts.statement: David J. Varricchio described the genus in 2002.
facts.quote: It was described in 2002 by David J. Varricchio.

facts.statement: The known fossil material consists of parts of a right wing, including the humerus, ulna, and radius.
facts.quote: Known from parts of a right wing – the humerus, ulna and radius bones

facts.statement: The only known specimens are housed in the Museum of the Rockies under collection number MOR 1113.
facts.quote: the only specimens found so far are housed in the Museum of the Rockies (collection number MOR 1113)

facts.statement: Comparisons with ground bird wing bones suggest Piksi was about the size of a common pheasant.
facts.quote: Comparando el tamaño de los fósiles con los de los huesos alares de las aves terrestres, se estimó que P. barbarulna eran tan grande como un faisán común

facts.statement: Its wingspan is estimated to have been perhaps 80 cm or slightly less.
facts.quote: con una envergadura de quizás 80 cm o algo menos

facts.statement: The animal may have weighed between 500 grams and 1 kilogram.
facts.quote: Puede haber tenido un peso de 500 gramos a 1 kilogramo.

facts.statement: Agnolin and Varricchio (2012) reinterpreted Piksi as a pterosaur instead of a bird.
facts.quote: Agnolin and Varricchio (2012) reinterpreted Piksi barbarulna as a pterosaur rather than a bird

facts.statement: Recent studies suggest affinities for the suborder Pteranodontoidea.
The species is classified within the suborder Pterodactyloidea.
The species belongs to the superfamily Ornithocheiroidea.
The time range for Piksi is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The bones were found in a silty claystone deposit.
facts.quote: The deposit in which the bones were found was a silty claystone.

facts.statement: The fossil site was inland, at least 350 km from the coast of the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: The location was inland, with the Western Interior Seaway's coast at least 350 km (220 miles) away.

facts.statement: The sediment likely formed from a small floodplain or ephemeral pool.
facts.quote: The claystone apparently formed from sediment of a small floodplain, such as an ephemeral pool.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Piksi is a pterosaur, as its humerus possesses features found in theropods but not in any pterodactyloid pterosaurs.
facts.quote: it has since been noted that the humerus of Piksi possesses features which found in some theropods but not in any pterodactyloid pterosaurs.

facts.statement: The species name barbarulna means "strange elbowed big bird", combining Blackfoot words for "big bird" or "chicken" with the Latin word for "strange" and the bone name "ulna".
facts.quote: Piksi barbarulna (meaning "strange elbowed big bird", from Blackfoot piksi, "big bird" or, specifically, "chicken" and Latin barbarus "strange, outlandish" + ulna, elbow)

rejected.statement: Piksi lived approximately 75 million years ago in what is now Montana, United States.
rejected.quote: It lived roughly 75 million years ago in what is now Montana, United States.

rejected.statement: The absence of fish and other aquatic animals suggests there were no permanent bodies of water at the site.
